trip_plan.totalNote: A three-day Bullseye Traverse: Stevens Pass to camp at Chain Lakes, drop packs at Bullseye Pass for a 4.5-hour side trip up Bull's Tooth's south side and continue to camp near Frosty Pass, then hike out to Whitepine.

days.title: Stevens Pass to Chain Lakes
days.objective: Camp at Middle Chain Lake
days.note: Follow the PCT past Lake Susan Jane and Josephine Lake, descend the Icicle Creek trail to the Chain Lakes junction, then grind up about 2,100 ft in 2.5 miles on the Chain Lakes trail to the lakes. Middle Chain Lake has secluded sites with views of the Upper Icicle peaks.

days.title: Bull's Tooth from Bullseye Pass
days.objective: Summit Bull's Tooth and move camp toward Frosty Pass
days.note: Climb to Bullseye Pass, drop packs below the peak, and scramble the steep southeast slope and a Class 3 traverse to beneath the summit. About one long pitch of Class 4-5 on the south ridge (40 m rope) reaches the top; three rappels from slung rocks return to the scramble terrain. Then continue past the Doelle Lakes to …

days.title: Frosty Pass to Whitepine
days.objective: Hike out to the Whitepine trailhead
days.note: Cross Frosty Pass and descend, with an optional steep side trip of about 1,150 ft to Lake Grace, then descend to the Whitepine trailhead for the pickup.

new_camps.name: Middle Chain Lake camp
new_camps.why: The usual first night: a long day from Stevens Pass ends in a lake basin right below Bullseye Pass, so Bulls Tooth is a short start away.
new_camps.permit: Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit required for overnight stays.
new_camps.notes: Reached by the PCT, Icicle Creek and Chain Lakes trails, about 10 miles. Camp well back from the shore.

new_camps.name: Frosty Pass area camp
new_camps.why: Sleeping near Frosty Pass after the Bulls Tooth day leaves a shorter final walk down to Whitepine; exact sites vary by party and by snow.
new_camps.water: Check snowmelt or tarns near the pass.
new_camps.permit: Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit required for overnight stays.
new_camps.notes: This night is not firmly confirmed; some parties stay at the Chain Lakes again before crossing Frosty Pass.

trip_plan.totalNote: Spend a full day reaching a 7,000 ft camp near the North Star-Bonanza col, climb the 16-pitch Cascadian Route and descend the Isella Glacier back to camp the next day, then hike out on day three.

days.title: Ferry, bus, and hike to the col camp
days.objective: Reach camp near the North Star-Bonanza col
days.note: The documented ascent used a full day for travel and the approach. Drive to Chelan, take the ferry to Lucerne and the bus to Holden Village, then hike more than 11 miles to a camp at about 7,000 ft near the North Star-Bonanza col.

days.title: Climb the Cascadian Route
days.objective: Climb to the southwest summit and return to camp
days.note: Finish the approach over talus and climb the route's 16 pitches, which gain over 2,000 ft. Descend the Isella Glacier on a mostly continuous walkway of steep rock and mellow moraine about two-thirds of the way down, then cross a notch in the south ridge back to base camp.

days.title: Hike out to Holden Village
days.objective: Return to Holden for the bus and ferry
days.note: Pack up camp and hike back out to Holden Village for the bus and ferry home.

new_camps.name: Holden Pass camp
new_camps.why: The high camp most parties use for Bonanza: it saves about 1,000 ft on summit day and puts the upper route within reach, at the cost of a rough hillside traverse.
new_camps.water: Snowmelt and small streams near the pass.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness camping rules apply.
new_camps.notes: Reached by the Holden Lake trail and a faint climbers path. Bugs are heavy in midsummer. Some parties stay at Holden Lake instead.

days.title: Day 1
days.note: Hike from Stehekin via the Agnes Creek Trail to Swamp Creek, climb Needle Peak's North Ridge, continue over the North and South Anonymity Towers, climb the Dark Glacier, and bivouac atop Dark Peak.

days.title: Day 2
days.note: Continue the connecting ridge crest to Bonanza Peak's west summit and then the main summit, descending via the Mary Greene Glacier.

camps_on_file.name: Swamp Creek Camp — the base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall and Lyall Ridge
camps_on_file.notes: About nine miles south of High Bridge on the Pacific Crest Trail and roughly three beyond Fivemile, this is the working base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall at 7,892 ft and the ridge between them. The unmaintained Swamp Creek trail leaves the corridor here and climbs toward Needle Peak's north ridge; the ground above is c…

camps_on_file.name: Purple Point and Harlequin — the landing camps, and the boat that decides the trip
camps_on_file.notes: Read this before any other site in the zone. Stehekin has no road to it. The only practical way in is the scheduled passenger boat up Lake Chelan from Chelan or Fields Point Landing, and the timetable, not your fitness, sets the shape of the trip. The slow boat takes roughly four hours each way and the express about tw…

camps_on_file.name: High Bridge Camp — the shuttle terminus and the base for McGregor Mountain
camps_on_file.notes: The bus stops here and the walking starts here, so almost every trip in this zone passes through it. Its own summit is McGregor Mountain, whose trail leaves the valley road near the guard station a mile or so from the bridge and is one of the biggest sustained climbs in the state: about 7.7 miles and 6,400 ft of gain t…

camps_on_file.name: Fivemile Camp, Agnes Creek
camps_on_file.notes: Five miles south of High Bridge on the Pacific Crest Trail through Agnes Gorge, this is the junction camp and the last comfortable night before things get serious. It is the departure point for Agnes Mountain — the West Fork Agnes Creek trail leaves here heading west, and it is the start of the standard approach to the…

camps.name: Swamp Creek Camp — the base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall and Lyall Ridge
camps.why: The closest established camp to the Swamp Creek way trail, so the climbing day starts at the turnoff and the walk out is shorter.

camps.name: Fivemile Camp, Agnes Creek
camps.why: Closer to the road end and easier to reach, but it adds about two hours to summit day. Use it if the boat or shuttle runs late.

camps.name: Purple Point and Harlequin — the landing camps, and the boat that decides the trip
camps.why: Lake Chelan landing camps, used the night before when the boat schedule makes you miss the trailhead. Not on a normal two-day plan.

camps.name: High Bridge Camp — the shuttle terminus and the base for McGregor Mountain
camps.why: A shuttle stop near the trailhead for the night before or after. It is too low and too far from Needle Peak to be a climbing camp.

trip_plan.totalNote: A serious 3-day trip built around one massive 21+ hour summit day: 14 pitches up the North Face to the Southwest Peak, a roughly 2-hour gendarmed ridge traverse to the West Peak, and a rappel/talus descent finishing well after dark.

days.title: Ferry, bus, and approach to camp below the pass
days.objective: Reach a camp just below the 7,100 ft pass between Bonanza and North Star
days.note: Ferry to Lucerne and bus to Holden Village, then hike the Railroad Creek Trail to Hart Lake before ascending rock-and-heather terraces to a camp just below the 7,100 ft col between Bonanza and North Star Mountain — a different approach and camp than the Mary Green Glacier routes use.

days.title: North Face to the Southwest Peak, then out along the ridge
days.objective: Climb the Soviet Route and traverse to the West Peak
days.note: An alpine-start, all-day-and-into-the-night push: about an hour of talus to the base, then 14 pitches of clean climbing up the North Face to the Southwest Peak, followed by a slow, gendarme-choked ridge traverse to the West Peak and a rappel/talus descent back to camp in the dark.

days.title: Hike out and catch the ferry
days.objective: Return to Holden and connect with the bus/ferry
days.note: Break camp, descend the drainage back to the Railroad Creek Trail (some bushwhacking involved), and hustle to make the afternoon ferry from Lucerne back to Chelan.

camps_on_file.name: High camp near North Star-Bonanza pass (~7,100 ft)
Holden Village
camps_on_file.notes: This is the base for Bonanza, Copper, Dumbell's eastern side, and the Railroad Creek walk in to Hart and Lyman Lakes. Its unusual value to a climber is that you can sleep indoors and eat three meals at 3,200 ft the night before starting up a 9,500 ft peak, which no other approach in this zone offers. The catch is that …

camps_on_file.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps_on_file.notes: About a mile above the village on the way to the trailheads, this is the answer for a climbing party that wants the Holden approach without paying village rates or fitting into a meal schedule. Being an open field it is exposed and has no shelter, and with only a site or two you cannot count on it if another party arri…

campsite_pins.name: High camp near North Star-Bonanza pass (~7,100 ft)

camps.name: High camp near North Star-Bonanza pass (~7,100 ft)
camps.why: Puts the north face a couple of hours away, with snowmelt water and exposed bivy sites, but it is a long haul with full packs.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: Indoor sleeping and meals before the approach or after the exit; not a place to sleep during this climb.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A low-cost field camp a mile above the village for parties arriving the night before; exposed and without shelter, and too far to climb from.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-3 day trip for most parties: ~19-20 miles round trip with roughly 5,700 ft cumulative gain/loss; camp sits near 5,900-6,300 ft on the old mining road, with a long (7+ hr) summit push on day two. Very strong parties have done it car-to-car in a single ~14-16 hr day.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp near 5,900-6,300 ft on the old Red Mountain mining road
days.note: Walk or bike the closed 5 miles of Chiwawa River Road from the Atkinson Flat closure to the Trinity trailhead first. From the Chiwawa River / Trinity trailhead (2,800 ft), follow Chiwawa River Trail #1550 along the old Red Mountain mining road, passing the Buck Creek and Chiwawa Basin trail junctions around 4,800 ft. T…

days.title: Summit day: Chiwawa Mountain via SW snowfield
days.objective: Climb Chiwawa Mountain (8,459 ft) and return to high camp
days.note: From camp, cross crusty morning snow slopes up to the broad saddle near 7,200 ft between Chiwawa and Fortress, then work up the southwest snowfield/talus with a short Class 2-3 ledge traverse to the summit ridge. Many parties tag Fortress Mountain's Class 3-4 east ridge from the same col on the same day.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Chiwawa River trailhead
days.note: Retrace the Red Mountain mining road/Chiwawa River Trail back down through the brushy lower miles to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps_on_file.notes: These are staging camps, not climbing camps: the point of them is that the drive up the Chiwawa River road is around twenty-three miles from the Lake Wenatchee end, the last twelve are rough gravel and dirt genuinely unsuited to low clearance vehicles, and doing that at the end of a long drive from the west side is how…

camps.name: Chiwawa Basin high camp benches
camps.why: Flat heather benches below the snowfield, with melt water, so summit day is short; the approach is steep and sites are exposed.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A car camp for the night before, after the long rough drive up the Chiwawa River road. It gives an early start but is not a climbing camp.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip built around Lake Chelan boat/Holden shuttle logistics: ~2,300 ft hike in to Copper Creek basin camp, a ~7-hr, 3,365 ft round-trip summit push on day 2, and a hike out to catch the boat on day 3.

days.title: Boat, shuttle, and hike to Copper Creek basin camp
days.objective: Reach Copper Creek basin camp (~5,600 ft)
days.note: Ride the Lake Chelan boat from Field's Point (or Chelan) up-lake to Lucerne (~4 hrs on the Lady of the Lake II), then the Holden Village shuttle bus up Railroad Creek Road to Holden Campground (3,300 ft). From there hike the Railroad Creek and Copper Creek trails about 3.5 miles up into Copper Creek basin and set camp …

days.title: Summit day: Southeast Glacier + Northeast Ridge
days.objective: Climb the SE Glacier and NE Ridge to the 8,965 ft summit and return to camp
days.note: An alpine-start day: cross the remnant Southeast Glacier (minor crevasses, usually easily avoided), find the easiest Class 3-4 gully/notch on climber's right above the glacier, then scramble the upper Northeast Ridge (mostly Class 3, with one exposed Class 3+ down-climb near a notch that trip reports flag as the crux) …

days.title: Hike out and boat/shuttle back to Chelan
days.objective: Return to Holden and catch the shuttle/boat down-lake
days.note: Reverse the Copper Creek and Railroad Creek trails back to Holden Village, then catch the scheduled shuttle to Lucerne and the boat back to Field's Point/Chelan. Boat and shuttle departures are limited, so this day is planned around their timetable, not the hike.

camps_on_file.name: Holden Village

Its unusual value to a climber is that you can sleep indoors and eat three meals at 3,200 ft the night before starting up a 9,500 ft peak, which no other approach in this zone offers. The catch is that …

camps_on_file.notes: About a mile above the village on the way to the trailheads, this is the answer for a climbing party that wants the Holden approach without paying village rates or fitting into a meal schedule. Being an open field it is exposed and has no shelter, and with only a site or two you cannot count on it if another party arri…

camps.name: Copper Creek basin camp
camps.why: The high camp under the glacier, about 3 miles above the road, with water and a short summit day, but a steep approach with a full pack.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: Indoor beds and meals before or after the climb, and a low start of 3,200 ft. It adds a long day if you sleep there between nights.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A field camp near the village for the night before an early start. Open and exposed with few sites, and far below the climb.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day backpack is the common recommended plan (~17 mi, ~5,000 ft gain round trip); very strong parties do combine it into one long car-to-car day (~10.5-11 hrs), often tagging neighboring Greenwood Mountain too.

days.title: Hike in to Upper Phelps Basin
days.objective: Establish camp near ~6,000 ft (established bivy sites cluster 5,700-6,100 ft)
days.note: Walk or bike the closed 6 miles of Chiwawa River Road from the Atkinson Flat closure to the Phelps Creek trailhead first. An easy, well-graded cruise up the Phelps Creek Trail through Spider Meadow, then a rougher push into upper Phelps Basin where the trail peters out to a bootpath. Camp here (rather than lower Spider…

days.title: Climb Dumbell Mountain
days.objective: Summit Dumbell (8,416 ft) via the Southwest Slope-South Face scramble
days.note: From camp, ascend the talus basin south of the peak to a notch just west of the summit, pick through two short cliff bands (the second via a dirty gully on the left, then class 2 ledges), then follow the ridge - easy but airy class 3 - to the top. Many parties tag Greenwood Mountain too via a connecting summit ledge be…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Phelps Creek trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach through upper Phelps Basin and Spider Meadow back down the Phelps Creek Trail to the car.

camps_on_file.name: Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin
camps_on_file.notes: About five and a half miles and 1,250 ft from the Phelps Creek trailhead at roughly 3,500 ft, this is the standard first night for almost everything on the Chiwawa side. It stages the Spider Gap crossing to Lyman Lakes and so serves North Star, Cloudy and Chiwawa; Phelps Basin half a mile above the head of the meadow i…

camps_on_file.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps_on_file.notes: These are staging camps, not climbing camps: the point of them is that the drive up the Chiwawa River road is around twenty-three miles from the Lake Wenatchee end, the last twelve are rough gravel and dirt genuinely unsuited to low clearance vehicles, and doing that at the end of a long drive from the west side is how…

camps.name: Lower Phelps Basin Bivy
camps.why: Sits right below the climb, so summit day is short, but sites are few and dry in late season; carry water from the creek.

camps.name: Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin
camps.why: Plenty of flat, protected sites with water about 5 miles in, which leaves a longer summit day. Go here if you want comfort over a short push.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A trailhead car camp for the night before after the rough gravel drive; it gives a morning start but is not a climbing camp.

previous_research.plan_conflict: Lower Phelps Basin Bivy and Spider Meadow are both filed as main; the plan's upper-basin camp matches the bivy, so Spider Meadow is the alternative.

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike in via the Buck Creek and Chiwawa River trails to camp at the ~7,200-ft Chiwawa-Fortress col, climb Fortress (and often Chiwawa) from camp, then hike back out.

days.title: Hike in to the Chiwawa-Fortress col
days.objective: Camp at the ~7,200-ft col or the 7,100-ft plateau
days.note: Hike in via the Chiwawa River and Buck Creek trails and climb cross-country to camp at the Chiwawa-Fortress col (about 7,200 ft) or a meadow plateau at about 7,100 ft below Fortress.

days.title: Climb Fortress Mountain
days.objective: Climb the East Ridge and return to camp
days.note: Climb Fortress, and often Chiwawa Mountain, from camp.

days.title: Hike out to Trinity
days.objective: Return to the Trinity Trailhead
days.note: Hike back out to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Chiwawa Basin bench
camps_on_file.notes: A flat heather bench in the upper Chiwawa basin between Fortress and Chiwawa, reached by a short climb from the end of the Chiwawa River trail. The usual high camp for the east side of Fortress and for Chiwawa.

camps_on_file.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds

camps.name: Chiwawa Basin bench
camps.why: A flat heather bench near the col, with melt water; it makes the east ridge a short day, though it is windy and a long haul with packs.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A car camp for the night before after the long gravel drive; gives an earlier start but is nowhere near the ridge.

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike in to upper Phelps Basin, climb Greenwood (and/or Dumbell) from camp, then hike out.

days.title: Hike in to upper Phelps Basin
days.objective: Camp near 5,700-5,800 ft in upper Phelps Basin
days.note: Hike roughly 5 miles from the Phelps Creek Trailhead to a camp in upper Phelps Basin at about 5,700-5,800 ft.

days.title: Climb Greenwood via the Dumbell col
days.objective: Summit Greenwood and/or Dumbell and return to camp
days.note: Climb Dumbell and/or Greenwood via the connecting col and ledge, then return to camp. Round trips from camp have taken roughly 8-11 hours.

days.title: Hike out to Phelps Creek
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Pack up and hike out to the Phelps Creek Trailhead.

new_camps.name: Upper Phelps Basin camp
new_camps.why: Puts the Dumbell col within reach for a short summit day, and the creek is close, but sites are few and small.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness camping rules apply.
new_camps.notes: About 7 miles from the Phelps Creek trailhead. Some parties stay lower at Spider Meadow for more room and a longer summit day.

trip_plan.totalNote: A remote 3-day backcountry trip by boat, valley shuttle and the Agnes Creek trail, with an exposed Class 3-4 scramble to the 7,911 ft summit on day two; not a realistic single-day objective.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach a camp near Swamp Creek, below Mount Lyall's west side
days.note: Take the boat up the lake and the valley shuttle to the bridge at the road end, then follow the crest trail south up Agnes Creek toward Swamp Creek. Camp near Swamp Creek to shorten the summit day; expect blowdown and possible stream crossings on the way in.

days.title: Summit day via the Southwest Ridge
days.objective: Climb the Southwest Ridge to the summit and return to camp
days.note: Cross Swamp Creek and climb through brush and open basin into the broad basin west of the peak, then up talus and old snow to the 7,300 ft notch on the southwest ridge. days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Break camp and retrace the approach trail back to the trailhead.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, ~21-mile round trip with a long class 3-4 summit day out of a Leroy Basin high camp; ~7,500 ft of cumulative gain, most of it on day 2.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach Leroy Basin camp
days.note: Walk or bike the closed 6 miles of Chiwawa River Road from the Atkinson Flat closure to the Phelps Creek trailhead first. Hike the Phelps Creek Trail then break off onto the Leroy climbers' path, which steepens sharply (around 1,200 ft/mile) into Leroy Basin. Parties report going through several liters of water on this…

days.title: Summit push via Freezer Pass and the SW ridge
days.objective: Climb South Spectacle Butte (8,392 ft) and return to camp
days.note: A long day: cross Leroy Pass and Freezer Pass, drop into the Ice Lakes basin, then traverse a loose, consequential stream-bed crux before gaining the southwest ridge on a scree ramp. The scrambling above is chossy class 3 (feels like low class 4 with the exposure) with several one-at-a-time sections to avoid rockfall.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead
days.note: Break camp and retrace the Leroy climbers' path and Phelps Creek Trail back to the car.

camps.name: Leroy Basin camp
camps.why: The only practical high camp on this approach: meadow sites and water at about 6,100 ft, giving a long but possible summit day over two passes.

name: Little Giant Pass – Luahna Col Route

trip_plan.totalNote: Cross Little Giant Pass into the Napeequa Valley to camp near Butterfly Butte, climb Chalangin via the north ridge and gully the next day, then hike out over the pass.

days.title: Over Little Giant Pass to Butterfly Butte
days.objective: Reach camp near Butterfly Butte
days.note: From the Little Giant Trailhead at 2,600 ft, ford the Chiwawa River and climb the Little Giant Pass Trail through steep forest and meadows to the 6,409 ft pass. Descend roughly 2,200 ft into the Napeequa Valley and follow the river, off-trail in its upper reaches, to camp near Butterfly Butte at about 6,200 ft.

days.title: Scramble Chalangin from camp
days.objective: Summit Chalangin and return to camp
days.note: Traverse past the Pilz Glacier, gain the north ridge and gully, and scramble to the summit, often adding Luahna Peak and/or Clark Mountain in the same push. Reverse the route back to camp.

days.title: Hike out over Little Giant Pass
days.objective: Return to the Little Giant Trailhead
days.note: Retrace the Napeequa Valley, re-climb Little Giant Pass, and drop to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Butterfly Butte and the Pilz Glacier basin camps
camps_on_file.notes: This is the climbing camp for Luahna Peak and Chalangin Peak and the Napeequa-side base for Clark Mountain, roughly eleven hundred feet above the Napeequa floor after the river crossing near Louis Creek. The benches around Butterfly Butte at about 5,850 feet are the comfortable choice and look straight across at Clark;…

camps_on_file.name: Napeequa Valley floor near Louis Creek
camps_on_file.notes: This is the way into the Napeequa for Luahna Peak, Chalangin Peak, the Napeequa side of Clark, and Tenpeak's east end. From the Little Giant trailhead the very first obstacle is fording the Chiwawa itself — the old bridge is gone and its remains are in the brush by the water, so the crossing is a wade and its depth dec…

camps.name: Butterfly Butte and the Pilz Glacier basin camps
camps.why: The climbing camp for Chalangin and Luahna: benches near Butterfly Butte with water, and the Pilz Glacier approach starts nearby.

camps.name: Napeequa Valley floor near Louis Creek
camps.why: A lower, warmer camp by the river after the pass; it shortens the first day but adds roughly a thousand feet and a longer summit day.

previous_research.plan_conflict: The plan puts camp at about 6,200 ft while the camp on file sits near 5,850 ft; the exact bench was not confirmed.

trip_plan.totalNote: Bushwhack up Thunder Creek to a high camp in Chalangin Basin, climb the snowy southwest face with a short 4th-class band the next day, and hike out on day three.

days.title: White River to Chalangin Basin
days.objective: Reach high camp in Chalangin Basin
days.note: From the White River Trailhead at 2,300 ft, hike the White River Trail to the Thunder Creek drainage. Leave the trail and bushwhack up Thunder Creek through slide alder and burned blowdown to a high camp in Chalangin Basin at about 5,100 ft.

days.title: Climb the southwest face
days.objective: Summit Chalangin and return to camp
days.note: Climb the south slope and southwest face on snow with crampons, plus a short 4th-class cliff band, to the summit. Reverse the line back down into Chalangin Basin and camp.

days.title: Hike out via White River
days.objective: Return to the White River Trailhead
days.note: Hike back out down Thunder Creek and the White River Trail.

new_camps.name: Chalangin Basin high camp
new_camps.why: The only high camp on the Thunder Creek approach; it puts the snowy southwest face right above you and saves a long bushwhack on the summit day.
new_camps.water: Thunder Creek and snowmelt in the basin; not confirmed.
new_camps.capacity: Unknown; expect a few small sites.
new_camps.permit: Wilderness permit required; check current rules.
new_camps.notes: Reached by leaving the White River trail and bushwhacking up Thunder Creek through alder and burned blowdown. Camp location comes from the trip plan and was not confirmed independently.

days.title: Day 1
days.note: White River Trailhead to a Boulder Creek ford camp (~3,700 ft); Day 2 (AM) — Boulder Creek camp up to a high camp in upper Boulder Basin; Day 2 (PM) — high camp to the Luahna summit via Clark Basin and Luahna Basin, then back to high camp

days.title: Day 2
days.note: High camp back out to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Boulder Pass and Thunder Basin, White River
camps_on_file.notes: This is the standard base for Clark Mountain and the reason Clark is a White River peak rather than a Little Giant one. From the trailhead at about 2,300 feet the White River trail runs flat for four miles, then the Boulder Creek trail turns east and climbs for another seven, crossing Boulder Creek at around 4,000 feet…

camps.name: Boulder Pass and Thunder Basin, White River
camps.why: A higher camp near the pass; it is farther than the basin camp and not used on this overnight plan.

new_camps.name: Boulder Creek ford camp
new_camps.why: The one night camp on this plan, at the Boulder Creek ford; it is a short walk from the cars and keeps the long climb for the morning.
new_camps.permit: Wilderness permit required; check current rules.
new_camps.notes: About four miles up the White River trail then to the ford. The plan then climbs to a high camp and out all on day 2, which is very long.

previous_research.plan_conflict: The plan fits two camps (ford camp, then upper Boulder Basin) and the summit and hike out into only one night and two days; it is not workable as written.

trip_plan.totalNote: A demanding ~24 mile round trip with roughly 9,200 ft of cumulative gain crossing two valleys — almost universally done as a 3-day backpack with a treeline camp on Berge's southwest side, not a day trip.

days.title: Approach to treeline camp
days.objective: Reach a camp at treeline on Berge's southwest side
days.note: From the Little Giant Trailhead on the Chiwawa River Road, climb switchbacks (500 ft/mi, then a steep 1,500 ft/mi pitch) to Little Giant Pass, then drop into the Napeequa Valley. Follow the Napeequa trail to where Berge's southwest-draining creek comes in, then grind up a steep, intermittent boot track to a flat spot a…

days.title: Summit day via the Southwest Route
days.objective: Climb Mount Berge (7,948 ft) and return to camp
days.note: A loose, exposed scramble: broken ramps on the west side lead to pumice slopes on the southwest face, then a traverse to the summit ridge. The true summit is the north high point (7,948 ft); the south summit (~7,914 ft) is a short side trip. Down-climbing the loose terrain is often slower than the ascent.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Little Giant Trailhead
days.note: Reverse Day 1: descend to the Napeequa River, climb back over Little Giant Pass, then drop the steep switchbacks to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps
camps_on_file.notes: Buck Creek Pass at about 5,800 feet is the base for three peaks in this zone that have nothing to do with Glacier Peak's own approaches. Helmet Butte sits half a mile northeast of the pass and is the shortest objective from here. Buck Mountain rises directly south across the valley and is normally taken by leaving the …

camps.name: Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps
camps.why: Belongs to the Buck Creek side of the peak, not the Napeequa approach this plan uses; only a party switching to the east-side approach would sleep here.

new_camps.name: Treeline camp on Berge's southwest side
new_camps.why: The plan's one camp: flat ground at treeline above the Napeequa that shortens the summit day to a loose scramble, then you drop back and sleep before hiking out.
new_camps.capacity: A few tents on flat spots.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness: free self-issue permit at the trailhead; Northwest Forest Pass for parking.
new_camps.notes: Reached after Little Giant Pass and the Napeequa Valley by a steep intermittent boot track beside the creek. Parties on other Berge routes have camped in larch-dotted bowls around 6,600 ft.

previous_research.plan_conflict: The camp on file (Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass camps) serves the Buck Creek approach; this plan's route sleeps at a treeline camp on the southwest side, so it is not slept at here.

days.title: Day 1
days.note: Drive to Hook Creek Boulder parking area, hike to Edward Mesa or alpine camp (5,000+ ft elevation gain, 6-8 hours).

days.title: Day 2
days.note: Approach The Mole base (40 minutes), climb North Face (3-4 hours), descend.

days.title: Day 3
days.note: Descend to vehicles (2-3 hours).

new_camps.name: Upper Hook Creek basin camp below The Mole
new_camps.why: Roughly 40 minutes from the base of the north face, so summit day is short and you sleep here again before the walk down.
new_camps.water: Hook Creek and snowmelt in the upper basin.
new_camps.capacity: A handful of tent sites in the basin and on Edward Mesa.
new_camps.permit: Alpine Lakes Wilderness: free self-issue permit at the trailhead.
new_camps.notes: The approach is a brutal, trailless slog of 5,000+ ft through alder and blowdown, so parties carry in and stay put. Ticks have been reported at the sites in early summer.

trip_plan.totalNote: A two-day, roughly 15-mile traverse over Mount Mastiff and Mount Howard to camp in the Upper Canaan Lake basin, then over Rock Mountain and out to US-2.

days.title: Merritt Lake over Mastiff and Howard
days.objective: Camp in the Upper Canaan Lake basin
days.note: Hike from the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead to Merritt Lake, then continue over Mount Mastiff and Mount Howard to camp in the Upper Canaan Lake basin at about 6,050 ft. This day accumulates about 6,000 ft of gain.

days.title: Climb Rock Mountain and descend
days.objective: Summit Rock Mountain and exit to US-2
days.note: Cross the Howard-Rock col and climb Rock Mountain's northeast side. Descend the South Ridge-East Slope past Rock Lake and out the Rock Mountain Trail to the US-2 trailhead; the full traverse totals roughly 6,300 ft of loss.

camps_on_file.name: Crescent Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The base camp for both Mount Howard and Mount Mastiff, and the natural halfway house on the crest traverse. It sits on the Nason Ridge trail one and three tenths miles beyond Rock Lake, reached by traversing a loose slope around the intervening ridge and dropping about three hundred feet, or from the other direction th…

camps_on_file.name: Merritt Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The eastern gateway camp. Its own trail climbs about two thousand feet in two and a half miles from around three thousand feet at the road, which is steep but short by the standards of this ridge, and it is by a wide margin the easiest way to get a loaded pack onto the crest. From here it is three and a half miles west…

camps_on_file.name: Mount Howard summit-area bivouac
camps_on_file.notes: Strictly a contingency and a preference, not a plan. Mount Howard is a day objective from a camp at Crescent Lake and there is no practical reason to haul water and a bag two thousand feet higher except to be on the crest at sunset and dawn, or to be positioned for a full ridge traverse taking in Mastiff to the east an…

camps_on_file.name: Rock Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The camp for Rock Mountain and the western anchor of the whole crest. The Rock Mountain trail leaves US 2 at about 2,650 feet and is relentless — roughly 3,400 feet in four miles of endless switchbacks on a hot, open, south-facing slope with no water and very little shade, which is the single most quoted complaint abou…

camps.name: Crescent Lake
camps.why: The natural halfway camp once Mastiff and Howard are behind you: lake water, and it leaves a short morning to the Howard-Rock col and the Rock Mountain summit.

camps.name: Merritt Lake
camps.why: The easy eastern camp with a big site and privy; sleep here only if you start late, then carry over Mastiff and Howard the next morning. Water is scarce east of it.

camps.name: Mount Howard summit-area bivouac
camps.why: A dry crest bivy for sunset and dawn views; you haul water and gear 2,000 ft above Crescent Lake, so it is a choice rather than a plan.

camps.name: Rock Lake
camps.why: Pleasant sites 1.3 miles west of Crescent Lake and close under Rock Mountain; used from the US-2 side or by parties who push past Crescent on day 1.

previous_research.plan_conflict: The plan puts night 1 in the Upper Canaan Lake basin (about 6,050 ft); no camp by that name is on file and parties are described camping at Crescent Lake, so the plan's camp could not be confirmed.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, ~16-18 mile round trip with about 4,400-4,500 ft total gain; most parties backpack in to Myrtle Lake or Cow Creek Meadows and make the summit a day trip from camp, often combined with Cow Creek Pass and Larch Lakes.

days.title: Hike in to Myrtle Lake / Cow Creek Meadows
days.objective: Establish camp for the summit push
days.note: From the Entiat River Trailhead (~3,150 ft), follow Entiat River Trail #1400 north about 4 gentle miles along the river to the Cow Creek Meadows Trail #1404 junction and footbridge, then climb 0.4-0.9 mi to established camps on the south shore of Myrtle Lake (~3,750 ft). Most parties treat this as an easy half-day and …

days.title: Summit day: Cow Creek Meadows to Fifth of July Mountain
days.objective: Reach the 7,696 ft summit and return to camp
days.note: Leave the maintained Trail #1404 above Cow Creek Meadows and climb open slopes/talus on the south side and south ridge to the summit — straightforward Class 1-2 scrambling with big Glacier Peak Wilderness views. Many parties tack on a visit to Cow Creek Pass and the Larch Lakes basin on the same day since the terrain i…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Retrace Trail #1404 down to the Trail #1400 junction and follow the Entiat River Trail back to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Larch Lakes meadow camps
camps_on_file.notes: This is the base camp for Fifth of July Mountain and the only one worth using for it. From the meadow between the two lakes the summit is roughly six miles round trip with modest gain, which makes it a comfortable day out from a camp you have already carried to. The approach is the Cow Creek branch off the Entiat River…

camps_on_file.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps_on_file.notes: This is the road head for the whole eastern side of the Chelan Mountains crest and the standard place to sleep the night before a long walk in. The drive is the thing people underestimate — it is roughly 38 miles of valley road from the Columbia, most of it paved, and getting here from the west side of the state is the…

camps.name: Cow Creek Meadows
camps.why: Meadow and small lakes with water, about two miles farther than Myrtle Lake but cutting about 1,400 ft off summit day.

camps.name: Larch Lakes meadow camps
camps.why: The highest base, near 5,700 ft, for the shortest summit day; it needs a much longer day 1 carry than the plan describes.

camps.name: Cottonwood Camp and the Entiat River road campgrounds
camps.why: Car campgrounds near the trailhead; handy the night before for an early start on the gentle river walk.

camps.name: Myrtle Lake
camps.why: The easy half-day camp on the south shore: a short pack in, but it leaves the full 3,950 ft of gain for summit day.

previous_research.plan_conflict: The Larch Lakes camp is filed as main, but the plan's short day 1 ends at Myrtle Lake or Cow Creek Meadows, so Larch Lakes is not slept at on this plan.

trip_plan.totalNote: An overnight trip: hike Wolf Creek Trail about 10 miles to Gardner Meadows and on to a high camp in Wolf Creek Basin, then climb the southwest slopes and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Wolf Creek Basin
days.objective: Reach a high camp below the peak
days.note: Hike Wolf Creek Trail about 10 miles to Gardner Meadows, then continue off-trail to a high camp in Wolf Creek Basin at about 6,200-6,400 ft below the peak.

days.title: Summit and hike out
days.objective: Climb the southwest slopes and return to the car
days.note: Climb the southwest slopes to the summit, reverse the route back to camp, and hike out.

camps_on_file.name: High basin camp above Gardner Meadows
camps_on_file.notes: The higher option for a party that wants to shorten summit day rather than take both peaks in one long push from the meadows. Heading north out of Gardner Meadows the ground rises to a small meadow basin at about 6,200 ft, and an old boot path leaves the main trail a few hundred feet west of the small stream to reach i…

camps_on_file.name: Gardner Meadows, Wolf Creek trail
camps_on_file.notes: This is the basecamp for both peaks and the way the great majority of parties climb them. The Wolf Creek trail runs roughly ten miles up the valley bottom from the trailhead near Winthrop to meadows sitting directly beneath Gardner Mountain, with North Gardner a mile further northwest along the connecting ridge. From h…

camps.name: Gardner Meadows, Wolf Creek trail
camps.why: End of the trail with water and flat ground, about 10 miles in; the base most parties use, but it makes for a longer summit day than the high basin.

camps.name: High basin camp above Gardner Meadows
camps.why: A small meadow basin near 6,250 ft that cuts summit-day gain, at the cost of a steep off-trail carry and less certain water.

previous_research.plan_conflict: The plan sleeps at a high camp in Wolf Creek Basin (about 6,200-6,400 ft), but the route page and other peaks' reports have most parties staying at Gardner Meadows.
